column2: Scent, flower, incense, lamp, food offering, circumambulation, bell, banner, canopy, spectacle, music and song,
having given cloth and the like to the god one obtains enjoyment and liberation. Musk, shilhaka, sandal and agaru likewise,
camphor, mustaka, guggulu and vijaya one should give. Having established it with a prastha of ghee at Sankranti and the like, he shares in all.
A bath is known as a hundred palas; anointing as twenty-five; with a thousand palas the great bath is declared.
Ten offences are removed by bathing with water; a hundred with milk; a thousand with milk and curds; ten thousand with ghee is desired.
Having given to the god maidservants, servants, ornaments, cows, land, horses, elephants and the like, one attains good fortune and goes to heaven with wealth and life.
In Kartika, having given jaggery lumps and ghee, the king becomes a heaven-dweller. I shall tell the twelve Meru gifts, giving enjoyment and liberation.
In the Meru vow on the Kartika full moon one should give a jewel-Meru to a Brahmin. Hear in order the measure of all the Merus.
Of diamond, lotus-stone, great sapphire, sapphire, crystal, flower-stone, emerald and pearl, the best is by a prastha;
the middle half, the lowest half of that; one should avoid deceit in wealth. In the pericarp one should place Meru, with Brahma, Vishnu and Ishvara as deities;
Malyavan is to be worshipped in the east; before that Bhadrasva; then Ashvaksha is said; Nishadha south of Meru;
Hemakuta, then Himavan: three; in the north likewise three: Nila, Shveta and Shringi; in the west Gandhamadana;
Vaikanka, Ketumala — Meru with twelve joined. Fasting, one should worship Vishnu or Shiva after bathing;
having worshipped Meru before the god with mantras, one should give it to a Brahmin: "To the Brahmin of such gotra, I give you the supreme Meru made of substance,
for enjoyment, liberation and purity, Vishnu its deity. In Indra's world, Brahma's world, Shiva's world, Hari's city,
having lifted his family one would sport in an aerial car, honored by gods." At other times too, on Sankranti and the like, one should have it given.
With a thousand palas one should make a gold Meru, with three peaks, with Brahma, Vishnu and Hara;
each mountain of it one should make with a hundred each; with Meru, thirteen mountains are renowned there.
At the solstice, an eclipse and the like, having worshipped Hari before Vishnu, having given a gold Meru to a Brahmin, he would long dwell in Vishnu's world:
for as many atoms as there are, he would long be king here. A silver Meru with the twelve mountains one should give with intention;
the previously stated fruit is his, having worshipped Vishnu and the Brahmin. A land-Meru, region, district or village,
having conceived by an eighth part, the remaining parts have fruit as before. With twelve mountains, in the form of an elephant-Meru,
one should give joined with three persons; having given, one obtains infinite fruit. A horse-Meru of fifteen horses, joined with twelve horses,
having worshipped Vishnu and the rest and given it, the king becomes one who has enjoyed enjoyments. By the number of horses one should give a cow-Meru as before;
with silk garments of a load each, a cloth-Meru in the middle; with twelve cloth-mountains, having given it, the fruit is imperishable.
A ghee mountain of five thousand palas of ghee; with five hundred for each mountain one should worship Hari;
having offered before Vishnu to a Brahmin, he obtains all and goes to Hari. Thus having made a part-Meru and given, one obtains the fruit.
A grain-Meru of five khari; the others of one khari each; all with three golden peaks, Brahma, Vishnu, Maheshvara;
having worshipped in all, or Vishnu especially, the fruit is imperishable. Thus by a tenth-part measure one should make a sesame-Meru;
its peaks as before, and likewise on other mountains. Having given a sesame-Meru, with kin one shares Vishnu's world.

Homage to you of Vishnu's form, homage to the earth-bearer; with peaks of Brahma, Vishnu and Ishvara, abiding at the navel of the earth,
agnipuran:212:34	lord of the twelve mountains, remover of all sin, devoted to Vishnu, peaceful, protect me in every way.
agnipuran:212:35	Sinless, with my ancestors, I go to Vishnu, Om homage. You are Hari before Hari; I am Vishnu to Vishnu;
agnipuran:212:36	I offer with devotion for the cause of enjoyment and liberation.
The lowest by a third part, in a tortoise-lotus; with a thousand palas one should make a wish-tree:
with root and trunk and leaves, with fruits and flowers; having conceived five trunks, the wise one should have it given in five parts.
The giver of this long rejoices in Brahma's world with the ancestors. Before Vishnu a wish-cow of five hundred palas;
Brahma, Vishnu, Maheshvara and other gods are established in the cow. The gift of a cow is all gifts, giver of all, giver of Brahma's world;
having given a tawny cow before Vishnu one saves the whole family; having adorned a woman, one should give: one obtains the fruit of the Ashvamedha;
having given land one shares in all — land producing all crops; giving a village, town or market-town one is happy;
performing the bull-release at Kartika and the like one saves the family.
Gandhari, Hastijihva, Pritha likewise, Alambusha, Huhu and Shankhini the tenth, are remembered:
these ten are declared the channels carrying the vital airs. Prana, Apana, Samana, Udana and Vyana,
Naga, Kurma, Krikara, Devadatta, Dhananjaya; Prana is the first wind, lord of all ten.
Prana enlivens the life by discharge toward filling; this one always fills, standing in the chest of beings.
Prana, resting on the living, with exhalation, inhalation and cough, since it causes departure, is therefore called Prana.
Apana leads downward the food of men downward; the wind carrying urine and semen is therefore called Apana.
What is drunk, eaten, smelled, blood, bile, phlegm and wind — it leads evenly through the limbs: the wind called Samana.
It makes the lower lip tremble, provokes redness of the eyes, agitates the vital spots — the wind called Udana.
Vyana bends the limb; Vyana provokes diseases; from the throat it is said to be Vyana by spreading in return.
Naga is said to be in belching; Kurma stands in opening the eyes; Krikara in eating; Devadatta in yawning;
Dhananjaya stays in the sound and does not leave even the dead. The soul goes out in ten ways; therefore it is the wheel of channels.
Sankranti, equinox, day-night, solstices, intercalary month, debt, deficient night and gain —
deficient night would be hiccup, intercalary month yawning, debt here would be cough, gain is called exhalation.
The north and south should be known; the left is called the right; in the middle the equinox is said, issuing from the two nostrils;
the Sankranti of it again is by union of places from its own place. Sushumna is in the middle limb; Ida is established on the left;
Pingala on the right, Brahmin; upward Prana is called day; Apana is night; thus one wind is tenfold.
The stretch standing in the middle of the body is called the lunar eclipse; the stretch beyond the body's principles they know as the solar eclipse.
One should fill the belly with air as far as desired; this is the breath-controller; the filling is the body-filler.
Having closed all doors, free of inhalation and exhalation, one should stand like a filled pot: that Pranayama is kumbhaka.
Then one should release the air upward with a single breath, the knower of mantra; joined with exhalation one should expel the air upward.
Since Shiva, abiding in his own body, utters it himself, therefore for knowers of principles that alone is called the recitation.
Twenty thousand, one thousand, six hundred — in a day and night the lord of yogis makes this count of recitation.
The Gayatri named Ajapa, Brahma-Vishnu-Maheshvari — one who recites that Ajapa has no rebirth.
Joined with moon, fire and sun, the original Kundalini is held; it is to be known in the heart region, in the form of a sprout.
There the placing of creation happens, by support of emission; one should meditate on nectar flowing in it, the best of sattvic ones.
The embodied is to be known as with parts; without parts, free of body. One who says "Hamsa, Hamsa" — the Hamsa is the god Sadashiva.
As oil in sesame, scent in a flower, so in a person's body he abides outside and inside.
Brahma's place is in the heart; Vishnu resides in the throat; Rudra stands in the middle of the palate; Maheshvara on the forehead;
the tip of the breath should be known as Shiva; at its end the beyond-the-beyond; the embodied is called fivefold; the reverse is without parts.
If, having raised the Prasada-sound, one recites a hundred, within six months, joined with yoga, he attains success, no doubt.
By knowledge of coming and going all sin is destroyed; within six months he obtains lordship with powers like anima.
Gross, subtle and supreme — the Prasada has been told by me; short, long and prolonged — one should mark the Prasada in three ways.
The short burns sins; the long is the giver of liberation; the prolonged in nourishing; adorned with a bindu on the head.
The "phat" at beginning and end of the short is beneficial in killing; the heart-mantra at beginning and end is declared for attraction.
